findings.problem: PacketWorkflow uses raw String and bool fields (status, is_validated, is_sent) making every invalid combination (e.g. is_sent=true with status not "sent", is_validated=false with status "sent") constructable.
findings.failure_mode: A packet can exist in contradictory states — is_sent true but status not "sent", or is_validated false while status is "sent" — because the type system cannot enforce the state machine invariant.
findings.fix: Replace status String and bool flags with a typed enum typestate (e.g. PacketStatus enum with variants like Pending, Validated, Sent) and a fallible constructor that rejects illegal transitions. Use newtype wrappers for id if domain rules apply.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a primitive lifecycle flag that cannot express the ordering invariant (e.g. packet cannot be sent before validated).
findings.failure_mode: Logic can set is_validated independently of status or is_sent, producing states where a packet is marked sent without being validated.
findings.fix: Collapse is_validated and is_sent into a single PacketStatus enum typestate (e.g. enum PacketStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }) that encodes the workflow ordering in the type.

findings.problem: status: String allows arbitrary values (e.g. "banana", "SENT", "") that have no domain meaning.
findings.failure_mode: Pattern matches or equality checks on status string will silently fail or panic on unexpected values, and no validation occurs at construction.
findings.fix: Replace String with a sealed PacketStatus enum whose variants encode the workflow states. If the status must be serialized/deserialized from strings, implement FromStr/Display on the enum in the shell layer.

findings.problem: PacketWorkflow has a public struct with all public fields — any caller can construct it directly with `PacketWorkflow { id: "".into(), status: "".into(), is_validated: false, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None }`, creating an entirely invalid packet.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid packets enter the system at any call site with no validation gate. There is no single construction point to enforce invariants.
findings.fix: Make the struct private, provide a `PacketWorkflow::new(...)` constructor that validates invariants (e.g. if is_sent then sent_at_epoch_ms must be Some, if sent then validated must be true), and expose only constructed instances.

findings.problem: mark_sent blindly sets status="sent" and is_sent=true on any PacketWorkflow, regardless of whether it was validated, without any precondition check or error return.
findings.failure_mode: An unvalidated or invalid packet can be transitioned to sent state, violating the workflow invariant. No typed error is returned for invalid preconditions.
findings.fix: Change the signature to `fn mark_sent(item: PacketWorkflow) -> Result<PacketWorkflow, TransitionError>` where TransitionError encodes why the transition is invalid (e.g. NotValidated). Validate that the incoming state allows transitioning to sent before mutating.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs mutation and string allocation ("sent".to_string()) instead of returning a pure new value from a validated domain type. The function has no error contract.
findings.failure_mode: Side effects and allocation are mixed into what should be a pure domain transition function. No error type means callers cannot handle invalid transitions programmatically.
findings.fix: Design mark_sent as a pure domain function operating on typed domain types with a Result return. Push allocation into the shell layer if the function is called from I/O boundaries.

findings.problem: id: String provides no domain constraints (format, length, uniqueness) — any string including empty or malformed values is accepted.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream logic assuming a specific ID format (e.g. UUID, numeric, delimited) will fail silently or panic.
findings.fix: Introduce a typed newtype `PacketId` with a fallible constructor enforcing format rules, and use it in PacketWorkflow instead of String.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> allows Some(0) which semantically may mean "not set" or epoch zero (1970), creating ambiguity about whether a packet was actually sent.
findings.failure_mode: A sent_at_epoch_ms of 0 may be interpreted as "not sent" by consumers, contradicting is_sent=true.
findings.fix: Use NonZeroU64 for sent_at_epoch_ms or validate in the constructor that sent_at_epoch_ms > 0 when is_sent=true.

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist in the crate to measure allocation behavior or performance of PacketWorkflow construction and mark_sent.
findings.failure_mode: Allocation patterns (String::to_string in mark_sent, potential repeated allocations) are unmeasured and cannot be validated against performance budgets.
findings.fix: Add a simple criterion or basic benchmark measuring mark_sent allocations for hot-path scenarios.

findings.problem: No profiler evidence (perf, flamegraph, cargo-flamegraph) exists to validate allocation hotspots or CPU characteristics of the packet workflow.
findings.failure_mode: Without profiler data, performance claims about PacketWorkflow cannot be independently verified.
findings.fix: Run profiler tooling and report results in the assurance bundle.

findings.problem: No allocation tracing (e.g. tracy, alloc-tracker, or valgrind --tool=massif) exists to document the allocation profile of PacketWorkflow.
findings.failure_mode: Allocation count and size for mark_sent (which does "sent".to_string() on every call) is undocumented and unbounded in tight loops.
findings.fix: Capture allocation evidence and document per-call allocation profile.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent performance
no profiler data for allocation hotspots
residual_risk: The type system cannot enforce workflow invariants because PacketWorkflow uses primitive fields (String, bool) instead of typed enums. mark_sent has no precondition checks or error returns. No benchmarks, profiler, or allocation evidence exist. Static review only; no commands run.
